name: MySQL Replication Topologies
tagline: Scaling MySQL reads and failover via GTID row-based binlogs across asynchronous, semi-synchronous, and Group Replication topologies.
purpose: Compare async, semi-sync (AFTER_SYNC), and Paxos-based Group Replication while preventing replication lag and split-brain dual-primary writes.

spark.summary: MySQL replication copies binary log (binlog) events from a primary server to one or more replicas to scale reads, isolate analytics, and survive node or availability-zone failures.
spark.keyTakeaway: Enable GTIDs and ROW-based binlogging as your baseline, use semi-synchronous (`AFTER_SYNC`) or Group Replication to prevent lost commits on failover, and enforce `super_read_only=ON` on replicas to stop split-brain.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** **MySQL replication** streams committed **binary log (binlog)** events from a primary server to replica relay logs so replicas can replay mutations for read scaling, backups, and high availability.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts MySQL Primary Binlog -> Replica Relay Log -> InnoDB Commit (App Write -> Primary Binlog -> Replica Relay Log -> InnoDB Storage); 3-Node MySQL Group Replication (Paxos Single-Primary) (Primary (RW) -> Replica 1 (RO) -> Replica 2 (RO)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Trade commit RTT against RPO and built-in Paxos failover. Enable GTIDs, `ROW` format, `WRITESET` parallel workers, and `super_read_only`.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore InnoDB gap-lock deadlocks, read-your-own-writes routing, and online DDL.

learningJourney.title: What is MySQL Replication
learningJourney.explanation:
**MySQL replication** streams committed **binary log (binlog)** events from a primary server to replica relay logs so replicas can replay mutations for read scaling, backups, and high availability.

Modern production MySQL mandates two baseline settings: **`gtid_mode=ON`** (tracking transactions by `UUID:sequence` rather than brittle binlog file/offset positions) and **`binlog_format=ROW`** (eliminating non-deterministic `UUID()` / `NOW()` replay bugs).

sectionDiagram.title: MySQL Primary Binlog -> Replica Relay Log -> InnoDB Commit

cards.label: 1. AFTER_SYNC Safety
cards.detail: Primary waits for at least one replica relay-log ACK before committing to InnoDB—preventing phantom reads and lost commits.

cards.label: 2. GTID Tracking
cards.detail: Global Transaction IDs allow any replica to re-point to a new primary cleanly without manual log-position math.

cards.label: 3. WRITESET Parallelism
cards.detail: LOGICAL_CLOCK + WRITESET lets replicas apply non-conflicting transactions in parallel.

sectionDiagram.summary: GTIDs + ROW binlogs + WRITESET parallel workers form the foundation of modern MySQL HA.

learningJourney.title: Why Replication Lag and Dual-Primary Split-Brain happen
learningJourney.explanation:
Two failure modes plague MySQL clusters:
- **Replication Lag**: single-threaded DDL (`ALTER TABLE`) or unindexed batch `DELETE`s serialize on replicas, spiking `Seconds_Behind_Source` to minutes and serving stale read-after-write data.
- **Split-Brain Dual-Primary Writes**: after a network partition promotes a replica, stale app pods keep writing to the old primary, diverging GTID histories.

ideas.title: super_read_only=ON Everywhere
ideas.description: Set `super_read_only=ON` on all replicas by default and revoke VIPs/security-group ingress on the old primary before unsetting `read_only`.

ideas.title: GTID Read-Your-Own-Writes
ideas.description: Route critical post-write reads to the primary, or call `WAIT_FOR_EXECUTED_GTID_SET()` on the replica.

learningJourney.title: Where MySQL Replication fits (and when to Shard)
learningJourney.explanation: Replication scales reads horizontally; it cannot scale writes beyond a single primary.

benefits: Offloads dashboards, `gh-ost` schema migrations, and snapshots from the primary.
costs: Asynchronous replicas lag under heavy write bursts.

benefits: Shard horizontally (Vitess / Citus) when write IOPS saturates one primary.
costs: Every replica must replay 100% of primary writes.

learningJourney.purpose: Scope boundary: identify where this pattern fits best and where simpler or async alternatives win.

learningJourney.title: Production my.cnf Baseline for GTID + Parallel Replicas
learningJourney.explanation: Enable GTIDs, `ROW` format, `WRITESET` parallel workers, and `super_read_only`.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```ini
[mysqld]
gtid_mode = ON
enforce_gtid_consistency = ON
binlog_format = ROW
binlog_row_image = MINIMAL
replica_parallel_type = LOGICAL_CLOCK
replica_parallel_workers = 8
binlog_transaction_dependency_tracking = WRITESET
super_read_only = ON  # Keep ON for all replicas until Orchestrator promotes
```
learningJourney.purpose: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Async vs. Semi-Sync (AFTER_SYNC) vs. Group Replication
learningJourney.explanation: Trade commit RTT against RPO and built-in Paxos failover.

benefits: ~0.3 ms local commit latency independent of replica network RTT.
costs: RPO > 0: unshipped commits are lost if the primary disk dies.

benefits: Zero lost commits on single-node crash; no phantom reads before replica relay ACK.
costs: Adds 1 cross-AZ network RTT (~0.5–2 ms) to every commit.

benefits: Built-in Paxos membership, automatic primary election, and split-brain fencing.
costs: XCom consensus RTT + certification overhead; 150 MB transaction size limit.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: 3-Node Semi-Sync / Group Replication + ProxySQL Fencing
learningJourney.explanation: Production MySQL clusters pair **ProxySQL** (splitting writes to Primary and reads to low-lag Replicas) with **Orchestrator** or **MySQL InnoDB Cluster (Group Replication)**, automatically fencing unreachable primaries before promoting a replica.

sectionDiagram.title: 3-Node MySQL Group Replication (Paxos Single-Primary)

cards.label: 1. Automatic Quorum
cards.detail: 3 nodes across 3 AZs tolerate 1 AZ loss without external Zookeeper/Orchestrator.

cards.label: 2. Chunked Mutations
cards.detail: Chunk large DELETE/UPDATEs to 1,000 rows and use gh-ost for DDL to keep lag <1s.

cards.label: 3. ProxySQL Routing
cards.detail: Shun replicas automatically if Seconds_Behind_Source exceeds threshold.

sectionDiagram.summary: Group Replication provides built-in consensus fencing, while ProxySQL shields apps from lagged replicas.
